items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had one gig, an afternoon gig that Rex Stewart took me on, too, because they were lacking . . . something had happened to their saxophonist.

ctx.x: About his style, I mean, it’s hard, of course, to describe it to someone who’s never heard it, and as you said, there are no records. But people like, as you mentioned, Roy Eldridge, and I think Rex Stewart mentions him.
Said he was doing things in the twenties . . . I think they maybe oversimplified it, but said he was like playing bebop in the twenties.

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: in Rex Stewart's book, I think that Rex said that the man paid me another $1.25 not to come back!

ctx.x: Just around the corner, yeah. And he took me to play this job, for which I was paid $1.25 -- and in Rex Stewart's book, I think that Rex said that the man paid me another $1.25 not to come back! I don't remember, but anyway, I started playing professionally, I guess you'd call it, some time after that.
Right. So that was, again, at about the age of 15?
